story: On 20 January 2023, Casey Rodarmor announced that inscriptions were ready for Bitcoin mainnet with the release of ord 0.4.0. The software offered a way to create and transfer digital artifacts using Bitcoin itself, without launching a separate token or sidechain. This card marks that public announcement, not the first experiment.

Ordinal theory provides a way to identify and track individual satoshis, the smallest units of bitcoin. Inscriptions associate content such as an image or text with a satoshi; their content is recorded on-chain in transaction witness data. The result brought a new collecting medium to Bitcoin, alongside its existing uses.

Inscription 0 predates the announcement. The Ordinals explorer records its timestamp as 14 December 2022 at 20:32 UTC, in block 767430. Its small PNG skull became an early visual reference. Here it is reimagined as a street mural, while a returning character from card 038 connects two chapters of digital collecting. The alley, artists and mural are fictional, not a documented launch event.

eggs.title: The skull mural
eggs.text: The large skull is an artistic reinterpretation of the image associated with inscription 0, not an exact reproduction of that original PNG. Its rough white backing keeps the idea rooted in a physical street-art metaphor.

eggs.title: The zero
eggs.text: The small #0 points to inscription 0. Its recorded December 2022 timestamp is earlier than the 20 January 2023 public announcement commemorated by the card.

eggs.title: A familiar punk
eggs.text: The red-haired character returns from card 038 as an intentional collection crossover. She is not a historical witness or a depiction of the inscription creator.

eggs.title: The second artist
eggs.text: A second figure works beside the mural, turning digital collecting into a shared creative scene. The figures and rainy alley are fictional editorial symbolism.

sourceNote: Sources: [Casey Rodarmor: Inscribing Mainnet, 20 January 2023](https://rodarmor.com/blog/inscribing-mainnet/); [Ordinals explorer: inscription 0](https://ordinals.com/inscription/0); [Ordinal Theory Handbook: inscriptions](https://docs.ordinals.com/inscriptions.html); [Ordinal Theory Handbook: inscription examples](https://docs.ordinals.com/inscriptions/examples.html). The artwork is fictional. INSCRIBED. is an editorial caption, not a historical quotation. The card date is the public mainnet-ready announcement, not the first inscription date.
